standard_prerequisites.name: Dimension of the local ring at a generic point, finite length of a zero dimensional local ring, and independence of length
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties, label properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring (proof line 1649); Algebra, labels algebra-proposition-dimension-zero-ring (proof line 1653) and algebra-lemma-length-independent (proof line 1655)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives that the local ring of the subscheme at the generic point has dimension zero, the second that such a ring has finite length over itself, and the third that the length remains finite over the larger local ring.

core_obligations: Part (1): at the generic point of an irreducible component the local ring of the subscheme has dimension zero, hence is a Noetherian local ring of dimension zero, hence of finite length over itself, and therefore of finite length over the local ring of the ambient scheme (proof lines 1646-1655).

Part (2): for a point where the dimension function attains the maximal value on the subscheme, its closure is an irreducible closed subscheme of the same dimension, hence an irreducible component (proof lines 1657-1662).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) via dimension zero and finite length (proof lines 1646-1655).
Part (2) via the closure of the point (proof lines 1657-1662).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that the length of the local ring of a closed subscheme at the generic point of one of its components is finite, and that a point where the relative dimension function attains the maximal value on the subscheme is the generic point of a component (statement lines 1628-1644, tag 02QJ-adjacent). The first part uses that the local ring there is zero dimensional hence of finite length, and the second is a direct closure argument. The dimension zero argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
